Without the answer options, I'd pick the objection that the calculus can't be applied: it requires knowing and totalling every consequence of an act, including far-reaching and unforeseeable ones, and no agent can do that. This is stronger than the measurement objection (Mill's higher and lower pleasures), which attacks the calculus's premise, whereas this one shows it can't guide action. Paste the options and I'll check which one best fits this reasoning.

CONFIDENCE: 45
